items.title: Emma Cortijo's Perspective Through the Joseph Petzval 27 mm f/1.7 Focus-Coupled Bokeh Control Art Lens
items.excerpt: Photographer Emma Cortijo shares her experience with the Joseph Petzval 27 mm f/1.7 Focus-Coupled Bokeh Control Art Lens. Blending stage lighting, movement, and experimentation, she explores a spontaneous approach to image-making shaped by the lens's distinctive swirling bokeh.

items.title: Memory Visually Captured: Bineesh Viswam on Exploring Joseph Petzval Focus-coupled Bokeh Control Art Lenses
items.excerpt: Bineesh Viswam, a Director of Photography from India, shares a documentary project inspired by the lives of Padma Shri award winners, framing their unique life stories with the signature look of Joseph Petzval Focus-coupled Bokeh Control Art Lenses.

items.title: Collecting Everyday Sceneries: Hong Kong Artist Apple Wong and Her Analogue Visual Diary
items.excerpt: Hong Kong artist Apple Wong uses the Lomo’Instant Wide Glass to create a visual diary of her daily life and travels, combining instant photos, sketches, and paper collages to record everyday life.

items.title: Creators in Focus: Filmmaker Justin Kaminuma on Embracing Experimentation and Creative Instincts
items.excerpt: Our next Creators in Focus edition features Japanese-American visual artist Justin Kaminuma, exploring his experimental approach to filmmaking and discovering the inspirations that fuel his work.

items.title: 7 of the Best Smallest Film Cameras You Should Know About
items.excerpt: Sometimes, the biggest personalities come in the smallest packages. This saying rings truer for the pocket-sized powerhouses featured in today’s list of compact shooters.

items.title: From the Archives of The Family Museum: Historical Tintypes Collection
items.excerpt: Archival project The Family Museum (@the-family-museum) is dedicated to the legacy of photography and how it's been used across the decades. To celebrate joining the Lomography Community, co-founder Nigel Shephard elaborates on a collection of historical tintypes.

items.title: Asian Glow’s US Tour on the Half-Frame Lomourette & Sprocket Rocket
items.excerpt: With their raw sound and dreamlike melodies, South Korean musical act Asian Glow has carved out a world of their own. We follow their US tour through Lomographic photographs, exploring their musical inspirations and how film connects the past and present.

items.title: Quiet Moments on the Lomo MC-A with Ryan Kemp (theworldisanalog)
items.excerpt: Film photographer Ryan Kemp takes the Lomo MC-A on Pittsburgh walks, sharing his approach to moody photography, film, and everyday shooting.

items.title: Trail Running with the Half-Frame Simple Use Reloadable Film Camera: Ding Yiqi's First Impressions
items.excerpt: A photowalk is common enough – but how about running and shooting? Lomography China handed the Half-Frame Simple Use Reloadable Film Camera Classicolor to Ding Yiqi, inviting her to document a trail run in Hong Kong.

items.title: Learning with Lomography in Leith
items.excerpt: Lomography in Leith, a research project by Dr. Huw Halstead and Prof. Carl Smith, encouraged students at the University of Edinburgh to see their city through Lomographic principles, gestural drawing, and self-reflective writing. Their results charted not just how Leith looks, but how it feels.

items.title: Community Gallery: Playing with Shadows
items.excerpt: Photography is known as the art of drawing with light, but its absence is just as much a medium for experimentation when we choose to play with shadows. In this Community Gallery, we explore the works of photographers who embrace the darker aspects of images.

items.title: Bertie Ocampo's Analogue Journal: Real Life Connections and Mindful Creations with the Lomo’Instant Automat
items.excerpt: Bertie's world is full of scraps, cutouts, stickers, and good music she translates into colorful journal spreads. She put the Lomo’Instant Automat to the test and added instant photographs to this equation, letting memories and real-life connections last a little longer on the pages.

items.title: Budapest on Lomography Film: Peter Seljan's Street Photography
items.excerpt: After picking up a camera following an eye surgery, Peter has mastered street photography while balancing a busy full-time job. In his latest project, he captured the vibrant atmosphere of Budapest using Lomography Color Negative 400 and LomoChrome Purple films.

items.title: Shot With Love: Film and Live Music by Julian Garcia
items.excerpt: Our next Shot With Love edition features Julian Garcia (@juliangarcia) and his deep love for documenting the live music scene on film.

items.title: The Camera That Brought Me Home: Marc Haeffner Tests the Lomomatic 110
items.excerpt: Photographer Marc Haeffner dives into pocket photography with the Lomomatic 110. In Part 1 of his summer series, discover what fascinates him about 110 film and follow his first shoot.

items.title: Between Life and Art, Between Photography and Love: Nur Aishah Kenton's Analogue Photography
items.excerpt: Australian-based artist Nur Aishah Kenton speaks about the process behind her analogue photo series, which translates intimate moments and shared experiences into captivating narratives shaped by reflections on identity, community, and being ‘in the world’.

items.title: Creators in Focus: Stitching Stories Into Motion with Tobie Tse’s Crochet Animation
items.excerpt: Meet Hong Kong-based multimedia artist Tobie Tse and discover how she turns crochet into moving images in this edition of Creators in Focus.

items.title: A Day With Marketer & Artist Yung: An Analogue Day with Friends on the Lomo’Instant Automat
items.excerpt: In this edition of A Day With, we step into the unique world and everyday life of LomoAmiga and marketer Yung, who has long embraced analogue photography. She spent the day with the Lomo'Instant Automat, capturing the opening of a colleague's solo exhibition on instant film.

items.title: LomoAmiga Mina Cho Snaps Lush Midsummer Portraits with the Half-Frame Simple Use Relodable Film Camera
items.excerpt: In search of the lush green vitality of midsummer and a touch of nostalgic early-2000s freshness, LomoAmiga Mina Cho headed to Yeouido Saetgang Ecological Park in Seoul with the Half-frame Simple Use Reloadable Film Camera.

items.title: Light-Filled Moments on Film: Lin Chao’s First Impressions of the LomoChrome Color '92 Sun-kissed ISO 400 120
items.excerpt: LomoChrome Color '92 120 Sun‑kissed is a favorite among vintage film lovers. We asked urban planner and photographer Lin Chao how he balances vision and instinct when shooting with it.

items.title: Three Photographers, One Model: Different Ways of Seeing With the Lomo MC-A
items.excerpt: Same gear, same model, same location, different visions. See how three photographers interpret one shoot setup using the Lomo MC-A and three Lomography film stocks.

items.title: A Day With Mineho Osawa: In Tune with Music, At Peace with Myself
items.excerpt: 2026-08-25 #people![Image 23: A Day With Mineho Osawa: In Tune with Music, At Peace with Myself](https://www.lomography.com/magazine/358818-a-day-with-mineho-osawa-in-tune-with-music-at-peace-with-myself) As the drummer of amenoparade, Mineho Osawa spends her days immersed in music. Once she steps out of the stage, her everyday life is shared with two beloved cats and the plants she loves. Using the Lomo'Instant Automat Glass, she captured these quiet moments on instant film.

items.title: Felix Kayser on East Berlin, Medium Format Film, and the Portrait as Dialogue
items.excerpt: In this interview, Berlin photographer Felix Kayser talks about his creative background, his sources of inspiration, what matters most in portrait shoots, and why he always keeps Lomography Color Negative 120 film in the fridge.

items.title: Drawing Memories: Inside Émilie Gleason's Analogue Journal
items.excerpt: 2026-08-23 #people![Image 25: Drawing Memories: Inside Émilie Gleason's Analogue Journal](https://www.lomography.com/magazine/358995-drawing-memories-inside-emilie-gleasons-analogue-journal) Instant shots, drawings, lists and endless small memories: comic book artist Emilie Gleason transforms a simple photo album into a personal chronicle of life, as sensitive as it is spontaneous.

items.title: Capturing the Invisible City: @filmlife_ww on Recording the Lingering Warmth of Hong Kong with the Lomo MC-A
items.excerpt: @filmlife_ww uses the Lomo MC-A with Lomography films to capture Hong Kong's vanishing culture. From street photography to neon signs, his visuals hold onto the city’s lingering warmth.

items.title: Poet-Photographer Satellite June on the Intersection Between Poetry & Analogue Photography
items.excerpt: Netherlands-based photographer and poet Satellite June takes us behind the scenes of her new book, where poetry meets analogue photography. It's an intimate look at the different layers of grief, and how film photography allowed her to bring those deeply personal emotions to light.

items.title: Half-Frame Stories with the Half-frame Simple Use Through the Lens of Guy (@dopamine.51)
items.excerpt: Shortly after the launch of the Half-frame Simple Use Reloadable Film Camera, Lomography Thailand sent the camera, preloaded with Lady Grey ISO 400 film, to Guy (dopamine.51) to put it to the test around Bangkok’s Old Town.

items.title: When Color Becomes Tool: Ishmael Claxton on His Methodical Use of LomoChrome Films
items.excerpt: 2026-08-21 #news#people![Image 29: When Color Becomes Tool: Ishmael Claxton on His Methodical Use of LomoChrome Films](https://www.lomography.com/magazine/357943-when-color-becomes-tool-ishmael-claxton-on-his-methodical-use-of-lomochrome-films) Dublin-based photographer Ishmael Claxton has been utilizing tones and hues from LomoChrome films to express ideas on race, identity, and meaning. He talks about his projects using these film stocks and the messages he conveys through them.

items.title: Two Days, Two Styles with Green (midori.pix) and the Lomo MC-A
items.excerpt: We chat with portrait photographer Green about his time with the Lomo MC-A and his experience shooting in completely different settings. He shares his impressions, creative process, and personal perspective on the camera after putting it to the test.

items.title: Yiran on the Joseph Petzval 55 f/1.7 Focus-coupled Bokeh Control Art Lens: “It's Not a Tool; It's an Expression”
items.excerpt: Some lenses just have a personality, and the Joseph Petzval 55 f/1.7 is one of them. Yiran took it out to the woods, the park, a small village – no fancy setups, just natural light. Here's what happened when she let this lens do its thing.
